say: Grow with discipline: one growth move, safe money, and a 90-day plan.
This is the video for module three of Women Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development.
Growth does not always mean a bigger shop or a big loan. It means more profit from a business that still runs well. You will choose one move that fixes your main limit.

say: Sell more to existing customers, with bigger packs, subscriptions or reminders before festive seasons.

Add capacity: equipment, a helper, a process
Add a product customers already ask for

say: Every investment needs a payback period: its cost divided by the extra monthly profit it brings. A short payback is lower risk.

card.title: Can Aisha afford a second fryer?

say: A second fryer and gas burner cost about 180,000 naira.

card.title: Can Aisha afford a second fryer?

say: 3 extra orders at 20,000 naira profit each bring 60,000 a month. So the payback is 3 months.

card.title: Can Aisha afford a second fryer?

say: A loan repaid at 36,000 a month for 6 months means she repays 216,000. The loan costs 36,000.

card.title: Can Aisha afford a second fryer?

say: That leaves 24,000 a month. Now the bad-month test. If only 2 extra orders come, just 4,000 is left after repayment.
So Aisha takes a cooperative loan for half and uses savings for the rest. A slow month will not break her.

say: Start with your own retained profit and savings. It is slower, but there is no debt.

say: Delegate tasks that are repeatable, easy to check and take a lot of your hours. Use a written task card and a simple work agreement.

panel.heading: What to hand over, what to keep

say: Keep pricing, key customers, quality checks and money. Blessing paid a helper 30,000 naira a month for ironing and used the freed 30 hours to win 2 office contracts worth 50,000. Without that plan, delegating would only have cost her.

panel.heading: What to hand over, what to keep

say: A SMART goal is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound. Blessing's: grow from 300 to 420 items a month in 90 days, with complaints under 1.5 percent.

Days 46 to 75: adjust using your numbers
Days 76 to 90: review honestly

say: Remember. Try quick wins before big bets. Work out the payback period, and borrow only if the loan passes the bad-month test.
If you fall behind, change the plan on purpose and write it down. Abandoning a plan quietly is the most common way growth stops.

panel.heading: What to keep from this module
items: Try quick wins before big bets
Payback = cost ÷ extra monthly profit
A loan must pass the bad-month test
Delegate only with a plan for the freed hours
Track a leading measure every week

say: Test your growth move with a payback calculation. Plan one handover and one partnership. Then write your 90-day plan with real numbers, marked as estimates where needed.
Now continue with the lessons below.
